root_cause.text: XDR decoding functions in SUNRPC auth_gss lack proper error handling cleanup paths, causing memory allocated via kmemdup() in gssx_dec_buffer() to leak when subsequent decode operations fail.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that gssx_dec_ctx(), gssx_dec_status(), and gssx_dec_name() functions perform multiple sequential decode operations that each allocate memory, but return immediately on error without freeing previously allocated buffers. For example, in gssx_dec_ctx(), if gssx_dec_name() succeeds for src_name but fails for targ_name, the memory allocated for exported_context_token, mech, and src_name.display_name remains unreferenced. The fix adds goto-based cleanup labels (e.g., out_free_targ_name, out_free_src_name, out_free_mech) that systematically free all previously allocated buffers before returning the error code, demonstrating that the original code lacked this structured error unwinding mechanism.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leaks in gssx_dec_status() by implementing proper resource cleanup via goto-based error handling that frees allocated buffers on all error paths.
intent_record.what: Replaced early returns with goto-based error handling labels that perform cleanup. Added error check for dummy_dec_opt_array(). Introduced four cleanup labels (out_free_server_ctx, out_free_minor_status_string, out_free_major_status_string, out_free_mech) that kfree() allocated buffer data and NULL the pointers before returning the error code.
intent_record.how: Previously, when errors occurred during XDR decoding, the function would return immediately without freeing allocated buffers (mech.data, major_status_string.data, minor_status_string.data, server_ctx.data). Now, all error paths converge through cleanup labels that deallocate these buffers in reverse order of allocation before returning, preventing memory leaks. The dummy_dec_opt_array() error case, which previously had no error handling, now also triggers proper cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak in gssx_dec_name by ensuring display_name buffer is freed on all error return paths.
intent_record.what: Replaced four early `return err;` statements with `goto out_free_display_name;` jumps, added a fifth error check with the same goto, introduced a new cleanup label that calls `kfree(name->display_name.data)` and nullifies the pointer before returning the error code.
intent_record.how: This change implements proper resource cleanup on error paths. Previously, if any of the five buffer/array decoding operations failed, the function would return immediately without freeing the `name->display_name.data` buffer that was allocated earlier in the function. Now all error paths converge at a cleanup label that deallocates this memory before returning, preventing a memory leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add proper resource cleanup on error paths by replacing early returns with goto-based cleanup handlers to prevent memory leaks in gssx_dec_ctx.
intent_record.what: Replaced direct return statements with goto labels for error handling in gssx_dec_ctx function. Changed 6 early returns to goto statements targeting cleanup labels (out_free_exported_context_token, out_free_state, out_free_mech, out_free_src_name, out_free_targ_name), and converted an inline -ENOSPC return to assign err and goto out_free_targ_name.
intent_record.how: This change implements proper resource cleanup on error paths. Instead of immediately returning when decoding fails, execution now jumps to cleanup labels that presumably free previously allocated resources (exported_context_token, state, mech, src_name, targ_name) before returning the error code. This prevents memory leaks by ensuring all partially-allocated resources are released when any decoding step fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add proper memory cleanup on error paths in gssx_dec_ctx() to prevent resource leaks when XDR decoding fails.
intent_record.what: Replaced three early return statements with goto labels that jump to a cleanup section. Added error check for dummy_dec_opt_array(). Introduced a multi-level error handling path that sequentially frees five dynamically allocated fields (targ_name.display_name.data, src_name.display_name.data, mech.data, state.data, exported_context_token.data) by setting them to NULL before returning the error code.
intent_record.how: Previously, errors during decoding would return immediately without freeing allocated memory, causing resource leaks. Now, any error in the decoding sequence triggers a cascading cleanup via goto labels that deallocates all five fields in reverse order of allocation before returning. This ensures proper resource cleanup on all error paths while maintaining the original error code return value.

grouping_result.intent: Add proper memory cleanup on error paths in gssx_dec_ctx() to prevent resource leaks when XDR decoding fails.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix memory leaks in GSSX XDR decoding functions by implementing proper resource cleanup via goto-based error handling on all error paths.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by implementing proper error handling cleanup paths in GSSX XDR decoding functions. The hunks specifically add goto-based error handling to free memory allocated via kmemdup() on all error paths in gssx_dec_status(), gssx_dec_name(), and gssx_dec_ctx(), which are the exact functions affected by the memory leak vulnerability described in the root cause.

When kmemdup() successfully allocates memory at line 103 (buf->data = kmemdup(p, length, GFP_KERNEL)), this allocated memory is stored in buf->data. However, the function lacks proper cleanup paths. If a subsequent decode operation fails in any of the calling functions (e.g., gssx_dec_status at line 330, gssx_dec_ctx at line 656, gssx_dec_name at line 545, gssx_dec_option_array at line 280), the error is returned without freeing the previously allocated memory. The function returns error codes but provides no mechanism to clean up allocated buffers, causing a memory leak.
